cases.scenario: Anchor distinct discussions to a text range, a table grid and an image. With a peer, insert and split text at range boundaries, move the image, then remove the anchored text, a boundary table axis and the image. Cold reopen and replay the history.
expected: Live anchors follow surviving characters and nodes according to the documented affinity and preserve their recorded quote. Removing the entire text target, a required grid axis or the node exposes the corresponding orphaned thread with its original quote and replies.
No orphan moves to an adjacent text block, row or image. Explicit reattachment records the authorized actor and target, and the restored reader agrees with the live room.

cases.scenario: Create two open threads, resolve the first, retract one reply according to the host policy, and find the thread in the comment archive after changing the underlying document and reloading.
expected: Open and archived filters show the expected thread states. The resolved thread retains its discussion identity, original anchor, attribution and permitted reply history.
An authorized reopen returns the same thread to the open view. Retraction visibility follows the comment policy and the document's accepted revision is unchanged by these actions.

cases.scenario: Mount a host discussion panel for one global document discussion and one discussion attached to a host metadata field. Read and reply through the panel with the editor unmounted, then mount the editor and reopen the panel after reload.
expected: Each discussion retains its own stable target, author, replies and resolution state. An authorized user can open the original target from the appropriate reviewing surface.
The external panel neither creates an implicit text-range anchor nor changes the accepted rich document. The host field discussion never appears under an unrelated field or document.

cases.scenario: In an installed shared room, grant one account comment-only access while an editor types. Create and edit a reply, save a second peer's reply, and exercise document Undo and comment Undo separately. Revoke the first account's comment grant and submit a previously prepared reply.
expected: The comment-only account can add the admitted reply but cannot perform a document edit. Each Undo affects only the permitted actor and history lane.
Revocation refuses the prepared mutation at the authority boundary. It does not add a new message, change the accepted document or remove already authorized replies.
cases.untrustedInput: Submit a reply containing markup-looking text and a claimed author label that differs from the authenticated principal. The server and recovered panel display admitted reply text as text and attribute it only to the verified account.

cases.scenario: Have two authorized participants edit the same existing message from the same baseline under a host policy allowing both edits. Queue one edit and a new distinct reply offline, hard-restart the client, reconnect and retry the same submissions.
expected: After synchronization, both admitted message versions are attributable, the reply occurs once, and any conflict is visible under the expected thread state.
A fresh reader and the confirming clients agree on thread state and message version IDs. The original anchor and accepted text are unchanged.

cases.scenario: In suggestion mode, propose a text replacement, a format change, a list restructure and an image replacement. View proposals as a second authenticated account, toggle between accepted and proposed presentations, and attach a discussion to one proposal.
expected: Each proposal shows its author, captured revision and the expected before/after effect. Accepted document content and raster bindings remain unchanged while decisions are pending.

The discussion retains the designated proposal identity and is visible to authorized reviewers. The accepted-only view omits pending content while the review view reveals the corresponding proposal separately.

cases.scenario: Have two reviewers submit conflicting decisions while a third user edits a disjoint block. Control delivery so Accept wins in the first run and Reject wins in a separate run. After reconnect, retry the recorded winning request and exercise accepting-user history in the first run.
expected: Each run records exactly one decision with verified reviewer attribution. An exact retry returns that result, a conflicting decision adds no effect, and rejection leaves the original document untouched apart from the third user's edit.
Undo and Redo affect only the accepting user's owned effect, preserving the peer's disjoint change, and the decision remains readable in review history.

cases.scenario: Prepare a formatting or text proposal and make a disjoint concurrent edit, then repeat with a conflicting change in the proposal target. Read an accepted-only export and, for a profile that enables it, a review-aware export of the same revision.
expected: The permitted rebase applies over the disjoint change and the conflicting target requires explicit review or revision. A refused rebase leaves accepted content and existing proposal history intact.

The accepted-only export includes accepted content only. The opt-in review export distinguishes pending, accepted and rejected states, preserves permitted attribution and includes neither private transport credentials nor queued mutation packets.

cases.scenario: Present a set of proposed text and formatting differences generated outside the editor. Select one to accept, reject a second and stage a third as a tracked suggestion. Repeat after changing a target in the live document.
expected: Only the explicitly accepted change appears in accepted content. The staged third change has its own reviewable identity and the rejected change has no accepted effect.
A stale target is identified before publication and unaffected live content remains intact. Diff view rendering does not give external change data editing authority.
cases.untrustedInput: Have the external change source return extra keys, markup-looking proposed text and an out-of-bounds range. Inspect the scoped diff and confirm invalid changes never reach native editing.

cases.scenario: Capture named snapshots before and after peer edits, then read a paginated version catalog while another version is published. Repeat an original publication, cold-restart the room and read with a freshly authorized account.
expected: Entries retain stable snapshot IDs, names, verified authors and source revisions. The ongoing page interval remains fixed and a refresh includes the later publication in order.
Retry exposes the previous entry exactly once and a cold restart reproduces its snapshot. Revoked users cannot use a known version ID to read it from the server.

cases.scenario: Enable the host's automatic version policy with a controlled clock and an installed room. Cross a configured interval without edits, edit and cross another interval, then save a manual named version between intervals and disable automatic capture.
expected: A quiescent interval produces no duplicate snapshot. Each enabled changed interval captures the admitted revision for that interval, coalesces changes according to policy and identifies the capture as automatic.
The manual version keeps its explicit name and source revision. Disabling automated capture stops new automatic entries without altering already retained snapshots.

cases.scenario: Compare two snapshots of one document with known text, formatting, table geometry and image-reference changes. Compare two distinct documents with equivalent structure but different internal identifiers, then compare each pair again without a mounted editor.
expected: The same-document comparison identifies the expected text, format, structure and asset-reference differences. Cross-document comparison follows the published matching rule without counting equivalent structure as a change solely because IDs differ.
Headless comparison gives repeatable ordered results and does not load image bytes or mutate either source or the current room.

cases.scenario: Preview an older named snapshot that uses a retained image. Receive a peer publication after preview and attempt Apply, then preview again and restore. Reopen the room and exercise the undoable restore history.
expected: The stale preview refuses without overwriting the peer edit. Applying a fresh preview creates a new attributed edit with fresh identities and the snapshot's immutable asset references.
Current comment threads and decisions remain current. Orphaned anchors retain their original quote, and missing image bytes are shown as an availability issue without deleting the restored binding.

cases.scenario: Use host-provided rewrite and generation actions on an explicit selection and on a block. Capture provider calls, reject one result and accept another. Edit a selected target while a repeat request is pending and try its late result.
expected: Each request contains the exact chosen text, ranges and instruction, with unselected paragraphs, account identity, images and review metadata absent. Provider invocation begins only after the explicit action.
The preview presents before and after text. Reject and stale-target refusal leave content unchanged, and one accepted rewrite contributes one undoable edit.
cases.untrustedInput: Have a test provider return an oversized result, an invalid object and a late answer after cancellation. Each is refused or discarded before a review or document mutation, according to the documented error.

cases.scenario: Invoke the configured translation tool on a selected section, explicitly choosing a target language, and request separate translations for two paragraphs. Review each suggestion, apply one, reject the other and compare stored text and formatting.
expected: Provider calls are scoped to the chosen text and named target language. The review view pairs each translation with its original text and target.

Only the accepted scope changes, preserving structure and other formatting required by the translation contract. Reject, cancellation and a stale targeted paragraph leave the rest of the document untouched.

cases.scenario: Run spelling, grammar and style review against a declared scope containing distinct known issues and multi-unit Unicode characters. Navigate issues using the keyboard, dismiss one, apply one and edit a different issue's target before acting on it.
expected: Only validated issues in scope appear in order, with labels linked to the expected ranges. Highlights are outside the editable content, and a dismissed issue changes no document state.
Applying the chosen correction is one undoable edit. A changed issue range withdraws its apply action without redirecting the change into nearby text.
cases.untrustedInput: Return one provider issue outside the requested scope, one range splitting a Unicode scalar and one message containing markup-like text. Invalid ranges are omitted and admitted messages display as inert text.

cases.scenario: In a host-enabled chat surface, ask about a selected excerpt, add a follow-up and request a rewrite. Collapse the conversation before the streaming response finishes, then reopen and review or discard its proposed edit.
expected: The provider receives precisely the context approved for the conversation, and opening or closing chat sends no undisclosed editor or review state. A streamed response stays separate from accepted content.
Only an explicit reviewed apply changes the captured target. The conversation and document remain usable after a timeout or cancelled response.

cases.scenario: In an opt-in completion profile, type at a caret, wait for a completion preview and dismiss it. Trigger another preview, move the caret or receive a peer edit before it arrives, then request and accept a current preview.
expected: Preview text leaves document content and cursor navigation unchanged. A stale or dismissed preview cannot insert text.
Explicit acceptance inserts the reviewed text at the current captured target as one undoable action, and observed provider requests carry only the configured prefix or selection scope.

cases.scenario: Use the host agent adapter to page through a bounded document read, inspect a selection and find a query. Test the model call interface using an accepted edit, an unknown tool, an expired read revision and a call with added arguments.
expected: Reads return the declared projection and continuation in document order, with the exact revision, bounded text and no implicit disclosure of comments, credentials or raster bytes.
Invalid inputs return the documented structured errors. Calls cannot bypass the host's configured tools, native grammar or exact target checks.
cases.untrustedInput: Check one extra property and one out-of-range offset using a controlled model response. Confirm no edit, queued publication or hidden context escapes validation.

cases.scenario: Have an agent stage disjoint text and format edits from one document read and preview them in the local review panel. Repeat in a shared editor wired to the suggestion queue and try explicitly proposed changes while direct mode is enabled.
expected: The local edits remain staged until accepted as one native publication and one Undo step. Shared review creates a proposal without changing accepted content, and always-review calls stay reviewable under direct mode.
Review can be rejected, and overlapping or stale targets are refused without applying part of the staged batch. Once accepted, a peer observes the same admitted change.

cases.scenario: Use the opt-in document server in an isolated fixture to create, list, read and archive a room with creator, owner, reader and unauthorized accounts. Compare the canonical reader snapshot with an installed client's current revision, then try archival while that client is connected.
expected: Listing and snapshot visibility follow current room grants. Canonical snapshot content and revision agree with the client after synchronization, and thread reads grant no mutation authority.
Owner archival refuses while a client is connected and succeeds after disconnect. The room leaves public listing and retained room bytes remain available to the authorized recovery workflow.
cases.untrustedInput: Send requests with mismatched principal credentials, disallowed origin and a body beyond the configured bound. Verify the documented error classes, no room mutation and no secret or internal path in the response.

cases.scenario: As an enabled service editor, submit an admitted command group against the exact revision read from the server while a client observes the room. Replay the request with its old base, try a command outside the allowlist, then revoke service authority and repeat with a fresh base.
expected: The first group is recorded once, attributed to the verified service writer and converges with the client's canonical document. A cold server restart preserves the accepted group.
Stale, disallowed and revoked operations produce distinct refusals and create neither a partial group nor an extra change notification.

cases.scenario: Create an isolated room, publish two edits within one debounce interval, create and resolve a comment and archive the room. Have a test receiver record then fail one delivery so the sender retries it. Verify the raw bytes with a controlled clock and separately try an altered body and an expired timestamp.
expected: The receiver sees the declared event types and a single debounced document change carrying the last revision. Each payload includes only the declared metadata and never doc text, comment body, credentials or secrets.
The receiver verifies valid timestamped signatures, refuses the altered body and expired timestamp, and observes the same delivery ID on retry so the recorded event is applied once.

cases.scenario: Configure a test endpoint to time out, fail and then acknowledge, while a second endpoint keeps failing. Generate enough events to fill the configured queue and restart with pending retries in the documented in-memory configuration.
expected: Logged attempts follow configured order, retry and capacity limits, with accurate success, abandonment and drop outcomes. Relay edits and reads continue while receivers are unavailable.

Only an administrator can read the delivery log. After restart the documented in-memory delivery boundary is observable, and the receiver can reconcile missed changes against an authorized canonical snapshot.
